seoTitle: Keyword Cannibalization Checker for Search Console
metaDescription: Paste a Search Console query and page export to find queries where several of your URLs compete, with the page that should win. Runs locally.
intro: Find queries where more than one of your pages shows up in search results, see how clicks and impressions split between them, and get a suggested primary page for each.
why:
Export the Performance report with both Queries and Pages dimensions (or build a CSV with query, page, clicks, impressions and optionally position). The tool groups rows by query, ignores pages below a minimum number of impressions and lists the competing URLs ordered by clicks.

Several URLs for one query is a prompt to investigate, not always a problem: a guide and a category page can both legitimately rank. Look for cases where the split is close, positions swap week to week, or a weak page outranks the one you want. Then merge, canonicalise, redirect or give each page a distinct intent.

No data is sent anywhere: the work happens in your browser, so you can use it offline once the page has loaded.
howTo: In Search Console, export queries with pages (or use the API) as CSV.
Paste the CSV; the header needs query, page and impressions columns.
Set the minimum impressions to ignore noise.
Review each query and decide whether to consolidate or differentiate.

faq.a: No. Two different result types for one query can both help you. It hurts when the pages are near-duplicates, swap places in rankings, or split links and signals.

faq.q: What should I do about a conflict?
faq.a: Merge the pages and 301 the weaker one, point a canonical at the primary page, or rewrite the weaker page for a different intent and update internal links.
